📚 DAILY MARKET EDUCATION
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🎯 ORDER TYPES EXPLAINED: YOUR EXECUTION TOOLKIT

Understanding order types is the difference between amateur execution and professional trading.

MARKET ORDERS - instant execution at current price. You want in NOW. Perfect when EURUSD breaks 1.0850 resistance and you need immediate entry. Downside? Slippage during volatile sessions can cost you 2-5 pips.

LIMIT ORDERS - buy below market or sell above. You set your price, the market comes to you. Example: GBPUSD trading at 1.3100, you place buy limit at 1.3050. You wait for your edge. No chase, no emotion.

STOP ORDERS - trigger when price hits your level, becomes market order. Classic breakout tool. USDJPY consolidating at 148.50, you place buy stop at 148.80 to catch the momentum move up.

STOP-LIMIT ORDERS - two-step precision tool. Trigger at stop price, execute only at limit or better. More control but risk missing fills in fast markets.

Real scenario: You're trading AUDUSD pullback strategy. Price at 0.6720, falling. You want entry at 0.6680 but only if it doesn't spike through. Buy limit at 0.6680 protects your plan.

PRO TIP: Use limit orders during range-bound Asian sessions, switch to stops for London/NY breakouts. Match your order type to market structure.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🧠 SMART MONEY CONCEPTS: LIQUIDITY SWEEPS

Institutional traders hunt your stops before reversing. Learn to see what they see.

THE SETUP - retail traders cluster stops below obvious support. Smart money knows this. They push price down, trigger the stops creating liquidity, then reverse hard into their real position.

RECENT EXAMPLE - NZDUSD last Friday. Clean support at 0.6150. Price wicked down to 0.6142, grabbed stops, reversed 60 pips by close. Classic liquidity sweep.

HOW TO IDENTIFY:
- Look for equal lows or highs (liquidity pools)
- Watch for quick violations with long wicks
- Check volume spike at the sweep level
- Reversal happens within 1-3 candles

TRADING IT - Don't place stops at obvious levels. EURGBP showing support at 0.8500? Your stop goes at 0.8475, below where smart money hunts. Or better, wait for the sweep, then enter the reversal.

Check USDCHF charts from Monday. Triple bottom at 0.8830. Tuesday morning sweep to 0.8818, then rally to 0.8890. Professionals sold retail fear, bought the panic.

SMART MONEY RULE: When everyone sees the level, institutions see the opportunity. Trade the reaction, not the obvious.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

💡 THREE DAILY TRADING TIPS

TIP 1 - MIDWEEK MOMENTUM SHIFTS
Wednesday often brings trend continuation or reversal signals. Monitor GBPJPY and EURJPY for directional commitment after Tuesday's ranging. First 2 hours of London session reveal institutional bias.

TIP 2 - CORRELATION CHECK BEFORE ENTRY
Before entering EURUSD, glance at USDCHF and DXY. If correlation breaks, something's wrong. Conflicting signals mean wait. Confirmation across correlated pairs = higher probability trade.

TIP 3 - ASIAN RANGE AS YOUR ROADMAP  
Mark today's Asian session high/low on AUDJPY and NZDJPY. London traders will test these levels. Break and retest = your entry zone. Respect the range until it breaks with volume.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🛡️ CAPITAL PRESERVATION: SURVIVAL FIRST, PROFIT SECOND

Your job isn't making money. Your job is NOT LOSING money. Profits follow preservation.

THE MATH - Lose 50% of your account, you need 100% return to break even. Lose 25%, you need 33% return. Every loss compounds the difficulty. Preservation is exponential edge.

HARD RULES FOR TODAY:
- Never risk more than 1-2% per trade on majors
- CADCHF or exotic crosses? Cut that to 0.5-1%
- Two losses in a row? Reduce size by half next trade
- Three losses? Stop trading, review your plan

POSITION SIZING REALITY - Trading EURCAD with 10,000 account, 1% risk = 100 maximum loss. If your stop is 40 pips, position size is 0.25 lots. Not negotiable. Not flexible. Math decides.

Wednesday psychology trap: You're up Monday and Tuesday, feeling confident. This is when overtrading starts. Stick to your plan. GBPUSD gave you 80 pips yesterday? Great. Today is a new day with the same risk rules.

Account protection beats profit hunting. The trader who loses less stays in the game longer, learns more, eventually wins more.

PRO REMINDER: Institutional desks measure success by risk-adjusted returns, not total pips. Think like the professionals who survive decades, not the gamblers who blow up in months.
